_note: Week of August 10–16, 2026 — Asian flair, same core proteins as usual (pork, chicken, salmon, shrimp, cod) reworked with soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic. This week's sauce card is a Soy-Ginger Sesame Sauce, used formally on Tuesday's lettuce wraps (swapped in for pita this week — same standing structure, leftover Monday pork plus a shrimp treat, just in butter-style romaine cups instead of bread). Saturday's vegetarian night is a sesame tofu and vegetable stir-fry. Sunday's breakfast-for-dinner is a vegetable and scallion egg fried rice. Reduced-sodium soy sauce used throughout given the kidney markers from Jake's recent labs; scallions are cooked into dishes rather than used raw on top, consistent with Laine's no-raw-onion preference. Kept the existing lower-purine, anti-inflammatory leanings — no organ meats or high-purine shellfish, tart cherries still in Jake's snack rotation. No mushrooms, lentils, okra, or eggplant; Jake's lunch stays saucy and reheat-friendly (broccoli, not spinach); Laine's lunch stays the standing tuna jar.

tzatziki.name: Soy-Ginger Sesame Sauce
tzatziki.note: This week's tzatziki-slot sauce — soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic, whisked together. Goes on Tuesday's lettuce wraps as the main event; a drizzle also works over the fried rice or the tofu stir-fry if there's extra. Makes about ¾ cup (8 servings of ~2 tbsp), keeps 1–2 weeks refrigerated since it's mostly soy sauce and vinegar.
steps: Grate the ginger and garlic directly into a jar or bowl.
Add the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil.
Whisk or shake until the honey is fully dissolved.
Keeps well refrigerated — shake before using since the ginger settles.

dinners.name: Teriyaki Pork Tenderloin with Sesame Broccoli & Rice
dinners.note: Not a fish night, so no conflict there. Homemade teriyaki glaze instead of a bottled sauce, so the sodium and sugar stay in check. Cook extra pork alongside for Tuesday.

ingredients.item: Pork tenderloin — Jake 320g, Laine 190g raw (buy ~210g extra for Tuesday)
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — Jake 1½ tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Honey — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine ¾ tbsp
Sesame oil — Jake scant 1 tbsp, Laine scant ¾ tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp

steps: Whisk soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil into a quick teriyaki glaze.
Cook the rice. Sear the pork tenderloin (both Monday's and Tuesday's extra piece, cooked together) in a hot pan 2–3 min per side, then brush generously with the glaze.
Transfer to a 400°F oven 10–12 min until the pork hits 145°F internal. Baste once more with glaze halfway through. Rest 5 min, slice.
Steam the broccoli, toss with a little of the remaining glaze and the sesame seeds.
Set the extra plain pork aside once cooled for Tuesday. Jake gets the bigger portion.

dinners.name: Pork & Shrimp Lettuce Wraps with Soy-Ginger Sesame Sauce
dinners.note: Standing leftovers-plus-a-treat night, reskinned for the week — romaine cups instead of pita. Monday's reserved pork plus a shrimp treat, quick-sautéed with carrot and scallion, sauced generously.

ingredients.item: Reserved pork tenderloin from Monday — Jake 210g, Laine 130g, sliced thin
Frozen shrimp — Jake 150g, Laine 95g raw, peeled, chopped
Romaine lettuce — Jake 100g, Laine 80g, leaves separated for cups
Scallions — Jake 35g, Laine 30g, sliced (cooked into the filling, not raw on top)
Sesame oil — Jake scant ½ tbsp, Laine ¼ tbsp
Soy-Ginger Sesame Sauce — Jake 1¾ servings, Laine 1¼ servings (see recipe card)

steps: Warm the sliced pork through in a skillet with the sesame oil.
Add the shrimp, garlic, and ginger, cook 2–3 min until the shrimp is just pink.
Stir in the shredded carrot and scallions, cook 1–2 min more until the scallions soften (not raw).
Spoon the filling into romaine cups, drizzle generously with the sauce. Jake gets more filling and more cups.

dinners.name: Teriyaki Salmon with Bok Choy & Broccoli
dinners.note: Fish night. Same homemade glaze approach as Monday, on salmon this time, with bok choy for something different from the usual broccoli-only side.

ingredients.item: Bok choy — Jake 160g, Laine 130g, halved lengthwise
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — Jake 1½ tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Honey — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine ¾ tbsp
Sesame oil — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake scant ½ tbsp, Laine ¼ tbsp

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Cook the rice.
Whisk soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil into a glaze. Rub over the salmon on a lined sheet pan.
Bake 12–15 min until it flakes easily.
Steam or stir-fry the bok choy and broccoli until just tender. Top the salmon with sesame seeds. Jake gets the bigger fillet.

dinners.name: Sesame Ginger Chicken Stir-Fry
dinners.note: Free night. Classic stir-fry format — chicken, a colorful vegetable mix, quinoa instead of rice tonight for a bit more fiber.

ingredients.item: Chicken breast — Jake 270g, Laine 170g raw, cubed
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — Jake 1½ tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Sesame oil — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine scant ¾ tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake scant ½ tbsp, Laine ⅓ tbsp

steps: Cook the quinoa according to package directions.
Sear the chicken in sesame oil over high heat until browned and cooked through, remove.
In the same pan, stir-fry carrots, bell pepper, broccoli, garlic, and ginger 4–5 min until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, add soy sauce, toss to coat. Serve over quinoa, top with sesame seeds. Jake gets more of everything.

dinners.name: Garlic Soy Shrimp & Cod Stir-Fry
dinners.note: Second fish night. Shrimp and cod together again like a couple weeks back, this time with a garlic-soy-ginger stir-fry treatment over quinoa.

ingredients.item: Frozen shrimp — Jake 120g, Laine 80g raw, peeled
Frozen cod — Jake 140g, Laine 95g raw, cubed
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — Jake 1½ tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Sesame oil — Jake scant 1 tbsp, Laine scant ⅔ tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake scant ½ tbsp, Laine ¼ tbsp

steps: Cook the quinoa according to package directions.
Pat the cod dry. Sear cod and shrimp in sesame oil 2–3 min per side until just cooked through, remove.
In the same pan, stir-fry bell pepper, carrots, garlic, and ginger 3–4 min.
Return the seafood, add soy sauce, toss gently to coat. Serve over quinoa, top with sesame seeds. Jake gets more of everything.

dinners.name: Sesame Tofu & Vegetable Stir-Fry
dinners.note: Vegetarian night. Pan-crisped tofu with a big mix of vegetables and quinoa — quinoa instead of rice tonight for extra fiber and protein.

ingredients.item: Tofu (firm) — Jake 260g, Laine 200g, pressed and cubed
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — Jake 1½ tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Sesame oil — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine scant 1 tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp

steps: Press the tofu (wrap in a towel, weigh down 10 min) to remove excess water, then cube.
Cook the quinoa. Pan-fry the tofu in sesame oil until golden and crisp on most sides, remove.
In the same pan, stir-fry broccoli, carrots, bok choy, garlic, and ginger 4–5 min.
Return the tofu, add soy sauce, toss gently. Serve over quinoa, top with sesame seeds. Jake gets the bigger portion.

dinners.name: Vegetable & Scallion Egg Fried Rice
dinners.note: Standing breakfast-for-dinner — classic fried rice, eggs carrying the breakfast callback. Scallions cooked in rather than used raw on top.

ingredients.item: Liquid egg whites — Jake ¾ cup, Laine scant ½ cup
White rice (dry, cooked and cooled) — Jake 55g dry-equivalent, Laine 38g
Scallions — Jake 40g, Laine 30g, sliced, cooked into the rice
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — Jake 1½ tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Sesame oil — Jake scant 1 tbsp, Laine scant ⅔ tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake scant ½ tbsp, Laine ¼ tbsp

steps: Cook the rice ahead of time and let it cool (day-old or fridge-cooled rice fries up much better than fresh).
Scramble the eggs and egg whites in sesame oil, just until set, break into small pieces, set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry carrots, bell pepper, garlic, and scallions 3–4 min until the scallions soften.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, stir-fry 3–4 min. Return the eggs, add soy sauce, toss to combine. Top with sesame seeds. Jake gets the bigger portion.

jakeLunch.name: Sesame-Ginger Chicken & Quinoa Bowl
jakeLunch.note: Sunday-batch, 5 containers, no fish. Chicken and vegetables stir-fried with a soy-ginger-sesame sauce cooked in, over quinoa — same reheat-friendly, everything-in-one-container format as recent weeks. Broccoli, not spinach.

ingredients.item: Chicken breast — ~3.5 lbs total (320g raw per container)
Soy sauce, reduced sodium — 1½ tbsp per container
Sesame oil — scant 1 tbsp per container
Sesame seeds — scant ½ tbsp per container

steps: Cook all the quinoa at once.
Cube the chicken. Sear in batches in sesame oil until browned and cooked through.
Add garlic, ginger, broccoli, and carrots to the pan, stir-fry 4–5 min until just tender.
Return the chicken, add soy sauce, toss to coat. Top with sesame seeds.
Divide quinoa and the chicken mixture evenly across 5 containers.

laineLunch.name: Cold Tuna & Black Bean Mason Jar
laineLunch.dressingNote: Olive oil + lemon juice, kept separate and added just before eating.

ingredients.item: Canned tuna in water — 1 can per jar (5 cans total)
Black beans — ~¼ can per jar, rinsed
Avocado — ½ avocado per jar, added fresh when eating
Olive oil — 1 tbsp per jar (dressing, separate)
Lemon juice — scant ½ tbsp per jar

steps: Drain tuna, rinse black beans. Dice cucumber and bell pepper.
Layer each jar: black beans → tuna → cucumber → bell pepper.
Portion the dressing into a small separate container per jar.
To eat: add dressing and fresh-cut avocado, stir, eat straight from the jar.

laineBreakfasts.name: Greek Yogurt Parfait
steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl. Top with thawed berries and flaxseed.

laineBreakfasts.name: Spinach & Feta Egg White Scramble
laineBreakfasts.note: Kept as-is — same-day cooked, so it doesn't have the reheating issue lunch spinach had.

ingredients.item: Pinch oregano, thyme, cumin, paprika, salt

steps: Sauté cherry tomatoes 1–2 min in a dry nonstick pan until they start to soften.
Add egg whites, scramble over medium-low until just set.
Toss in spinach at the end. Top with feta and a pinch of spice mix.

laineBreakfasts.name: Birch Benders Waffles + Berries
laineBreakfasts.note: Standing Sunday-morning waffles, separate from Sunday's breakfast-for-dinner — unchanged.

ingredients.item: Birch Benders pancake/waffle mix — ½ cup dry

steps: Mix batter: mix + egg whites + water per package. Stir in flaxseed.
Cook in a preheated waffle iron 3–4 min until crisp.
Top with thawed berries.

laineSnacks.name: Cucumber + Hummus
laineSnacks.desc: ¾ cucumber sliced + hummus for dipping.

laineSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt + Berries
laineSnacks.desc: 1 Oikos Triple Zero + small handful thawed berries.

jakeSnacks.name: Cottage Cheese + Tart Cherries
jakeSnacks.desc: 1 cup cottage cheese + 1 cup frozen tart cherries, thawed — the uric-acid-friendly swap from last week, kept in.

jakeSnacks.name: Roasted Chickpeas + Almonds
jakeSnacks.desc: ¼ cup roasted chickpeas + a small handful of almonds.

jakeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt + Almonds
jakeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain Greek yogurt + a small handful of almonds.

Quinoa (dry) — ~1.2 lb needed (Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Jake's lunch)
